summary: Two shared-infra hardening items from the myidsan productization plan's Phase 4 (Operability), both suite-wide since they live in infra/db and infra/apphost, not any one app. First, a connection-pool budget for the Postgres/MariaDB client/server DB engines: a new db.pool config block (maxOpenConns, maxIdleConns, maxLifetimeSeconds, maxIdleTimeSeconds, plus an explicit unlimited escape hatch) is applied via dbsql.ApplyPool right after sql.Open, before Ping, in both engines' NewDbCrud. The point is the default: Go's database/sql defaults to unlimited open connections, so a traffic burst could previously exhaust a shared database server's entire connection budget and take down every other application on it, not just this one; an absent/zero pool config now yields a bounded pool (25 open / 5 idle / 30-minute lifetime) instead. ApplyPool also clamps maxIdleConns down to maxOpenConns when misconfigured (database/sql would otherwise silently reduce it while the config kept claiming an unhonoured number), and always sets a lifetime bound even in the unlimited case. SQLite is unaffected -- it stays pinned to a single connection, a correctness constraint (concurrent writers to one file deadlock), not a tunable. Second, a startup statement of the HA/shared-state boundary: infra/apphost now logs, once per boot (warnSharedStateBoundary), whether the session cache is shared (redis -- confirms the app can run behind a load balancer) or per-process (states plainly that the instance is single-instance only, names the consequence -- users signed out on every load-balancer switch, all sessions lost on restart -- and the fix). A distributed transaction lock configured alongside a per-process cache logs a WARNING, since a distributed lock only makes sense with more than one instance and pairing it with a per-process session cache is a self-inconsistent deployment. docs/MYIDSAN_PRODUCTIZATION_PLAN.md sections 4.2 and 4.3 are updated to reflect this (4.3's connection-pool bullet is done; its log-file-size-cap bullet remains outstanding, and a prior inaccurate claim there -- that log cleanup only prunes DB rows, not files on disk -- is corrected).
compatibility: Existing Postgres/MariaDB installs move from an unbounded connection pool to a bounded 25-connection default per process/instance -- this is a behavior change. Most deployments will see no difference since 25 sits well under typical database server limits (e.g. Postgres's common max_connections=100), but an operator running a high-concurrency deployment, or multiple instances against the same database server, should review and raise db.pool.maxOpenConns (and, if truly unbounded is wanted, set db.pool.unlimited=true) rather than relying on the old implicit unlimited default. SQLite-backed installs are entirely unaffected. The shared-state boundary log is informational only -- it changes nothing at runtime, adds one or two log lines at startup, and requires no config change; existing single-instance deployments will simply now see the single-instance-only statement instead of silence.
